To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the contextualisation process should be: (i) more methodical and structured; (ii) more transparent and accountable; (iii) more robust; (iv) better able to address and mitigate the managerial risk of the equilibrium of contextualisation being unduly influenced by decision-makers; (v) better able to protect the integrity of scientific methods; and (vi) more effective in delivering the information that is needed by decision-makers.

(1) the contextualisation of volcanic hazard assessments is an unavoidable managerial hazard that needs to be mitigated; (2) quality standards for the contextualising of hazard assessments need to be developed; (3) the proposed quality standards are a pragmatic response to the realities of the hazard-risk interface; and (4), in the absence of a formal regulatory framework, the proposed quality standards offer the possibility of more robust hazard assessments.

quality assurance standards for volcanic hazard assessment should be developed and applied in order to ensure that the contextualisation process is methodical, that it is not influenced by decision-maker demands, and that the resulting hazard assessments are robust enough to withstand legal scrutiny.

quality standards are necessary to ensure that hazard assessments are sufficiently robust to be fit for purpose.
the quality assurance of hazard assessments should be a collaborative effort between volcanologists and their users.

the quality of volcanic hazard assessments should be enhanced by the adoption of a more methodical approach to contextualisation, one that is driven by the needs and sentiments of the users of hazard assessments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality assurance of hazard assessments should be based upon a more methodical approach to the contextualisation of hazard assessments.

the quality assurance standards proposed here are designed to facilitate a more systematic and methodical approach to the contextualisation of hazard assessments and that they are intended to support the development of a more effective, efficient and equitable approach to risk governance.

the quality standards and code of practice we propose would help to ensure that volcanic hazard assessments are robust enough to be legally defensible, that they are fit for the purpose of decision-making, and that they are not unduly influenced by any particular interest group.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quality of hazard assessments can be enhanced by a more structured approach, which is not necessarily in conflict with traditional scientific methodologies and can mitigate the managerial hazards of the interface.
volcanologists must adopt quality standards for the contextualization of their hazard assessments.

the quality assurance of contextualisation should be considered as a matter of urgency by the international volcanological community and that the adoption of our proposed quality standards would be a positive first step.
